title: IMPRESS-A: the API and the loop

acts.name: Functionality
acts.question: what can you write against this that you cannot write against a pipeline?
acts.gap: every toolkit that exists is one of the four real stages of a single chain, plus mocks, and nobody outside this package has authored either a toolkit or a policy

acts.name: Performance
acts.question: what does the loop cost, and where does it serialise?
acts.gap: no concurrent run and no serial baseline anywhere in the deck, so nothing divides into a speedup - and the stages were mocks, so this times the ENGINE and never the science

acts.name: Usability
acts.question: application, platform, or component?
acts.gap: nothing outside this package has ever driven a campaign, and `--model C` with no caller falls back to model D after 5 s instead of failing

orders.name: A · full
orders.fits: a 35-minute slot, or a working session where questions land inline

orders.name: B · default
orders.fits: a 30-minute slot: drops the loop/driver slide, the intent seam, the task-agent phases and the layering test. Each is recoverable in a sentence, and 5 still carries the map

orders.name: C · hard twenty
orders.fits: a hard 20 that leaves room for discussion: the framing, the three dividers, one surface per act, both measured slides, the interlock finding, status and asks

protect: **Protect 2, 3, 12, 15, 16, 17, 22 and 23.** Two and three are what buy the rest of the deck (the caveats at minute two and the named weak dimension); 12, 15 and 17 are the only slides carrying evidence from a real run; 16 is what keeps the performance act honest; 22 is status and 23 is the asks. Never cut a divider - a cut deck without them is a list of slides. Backups B1 (compute patterns) and B2 (the type lattice) are out of every order; do not put them back to fill time.
say_out_loud: that nothing outside this package has ever driven a campaign, so the component claim is empty and the control plane is the most carefully built unused thing in here; that `replicas > 1` DOES run - the mock campaign in this deck ran two lineages - and what has never run is `replicas > 1` on the real six-stage chain (backlog A10); that every stage in the measured run was a mock, so the timings are the engine and never the science; and that the 31% acceptance figure on slide 16 is transcribed from the project's Delta run archive, not mined from this checkout.
